rail_guard.text: Blackpool North. Trains to everywhere you've been, and on Fridays in summer, every hen do in the North West.
All aboard! Mind the gap and the inflatable flamingo.

bp_rock_seller.text: Rock! Real Blackpool rock, with BLACKPOOL all the way through. Snap it anywhere and it still says Blackpool. Unlike my ex.
The letters are made by hand in a big fat slab, then the whole thing's rolled and pulled thin until the writing is tiny. Like a sugary sausage with a message.

bp_landlady.text: Sea View Guest House, love. No sea view, mind, but there's a picture of the sea in the hall.
In the old days it was house rules: breakfast at eight, out by ten, not back till teatime whatever the weather. Wakes Week, the whole of Oldham stayed on this street.

bp_sandgrownun.text: Sandgrown'un, me. Born and bred in Blackpool. Visitors come for a weekend. We have to live with the lights every autumn. Lovely, it is. You can read in bed with the curtains open.
Get yourself a chippy tea: fish, chips and mushy peas, or a pea wet if you're proper. Then a barm cake. Then the Tower. In that order.

then.text: South, love. Nose down, tail swishing. Follow the hoofprints.

else.text: Bramble? Jack's donkey? I saw her trotting south along the sands this morning, nose down, like she'd smelt summat green.
She'll be halfway to Southport by now. Or Formby. Donkeys love a vegetable patch.
Ninety-nine with a flake, love? Strawberry sauce is extra and so is sympathy.
Ice cream on Central Pier since before I was born. My dad sold it, his mum sold it. We've never once sold a hot one.

then.text: Fuses to Doreen, bulbs from Southport, then a celebrity. Doreen's got you running about like the last tram at midnight.
Doreen wants the spare fuses from my cab? She'll have to earn them. Well, you will. Beat me fair and square, like the old timetable, and they're yours.
Right. A deal's a deal. One box of fuses, bit greasy, and some advice: Doreen's short of bulbs too. Every year. Try Southport Pier, the keeper keeps a crate.

else.text: Blackpool trams, since 1885. Older than the Tower! Electric from the start, too, from a conduit in the road at first, before the overhead wires.
I drive a Balloon on heritage days. Upstairs at the front, on the prom, with the lights on. Best seat in Lancashire.

then.text: Ladies and gentlemen, boys and girls, hen dos and stag dos! Our celebrity is stuck on the M55, so tonight, please welcome a very special stand-in...
...{player}! Ten! Nine! Eight! Oh, they've done it early. Never mind!
You pull the big brass lever. Six miles of lights come on in a rush, the Tower blazes from top to toe, and the whole promenade goes 'ooooh'.
Every bulb lit! Not one fuse gone! You're a star, {player}. Here, a little thank you from the depot.

else.text: Not yet, love! You can't switch on the Illuminations in broad daylight. Come back at dusk, when the sky goes purple over the Irish Sea.
Testing, testing. One, two. Is this thing on? It's the switch-on soon, and the celebrity's been held up on the motorway. Again.
Doreen at the depot's running about like a headless chicken. You could do worse than ask her what she needs.

then.text: Bramble's been as good as gold since. Well, she's eaten a hat. But it was a kiss-me-quick hat, so it's practically food.
Bramble! You daft article! Where've you been? Eating asparagus in Formby? Twenty miles for a vegetable!
Thank you, love. Honestly. Here, take this. It's one of her old shoes, for luck, the right way up so the luck doesn't fall out.

South, you reckon? Along the sands towards Southport? The tide's out, she could walk to Formby without getting her hooves wet. Could you go after her? She'll come to anyone with a carrot. Or anyone, frankly.
Have you asked along the beach? Somebody on Central Pier must've seen a donkey walk past. They're not easy to miss.

else.text: You haven't seen a donkey, have you? Grey, about this high, answers to Bramble. Well, she doesn't answer. But it's her name.
She slipped her halter at dinner time while I was counting the takings. Twenty-odd years on these sands and I've never lost one. Would you ask about for me?

blackpool_bowler.text: Mind the crown. It has seen off better bowlers than you, and a few worse ones who thought they knew better.
